title: ControlFusion: A Controllable Image Fusion Network with Language-Vision De

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3, paragraph after Eq. (1) describing DDL-12 construction
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states they selected 2,050 high-quality clear images and used the degraded imaging model to synthesize degraded images with 12 types and 4 levels of degradation, resulting in approximately 48,000 training and 4,800 test image pairs. 52,800 total pairs with 12×4=48 versions per source image would require 52,800/48 = 1,100 source images, not 2,050. The reported number of source images contradicts the total number of pairs.

The text reads: 'd(x) refers to the scene depth, estimated by DepthAnything-V2 [40].' Reference [40] is 'Syed Waqas Zamir, Aditya Arora, Salman Khan, ...; Restormer: Efficient transformer for high-resolution image restoration.' This is not DepthAnything-V2; the citation is incorrect and does not support the claimed depth estimation method.

The paragraph says: '...our approach uniquely includes pre-enhancement by several SOTA image restoration algorithms tailored to each degradation type.' ControlFusion is an end‑to‑end restoration‑fusion network; it does not use external pre‑enhancement algorithms. This statement misrepresents the experimental setup and contradicts the described method. It also creates confusion about whether the reported results for ControlFusion in Table 2 used an additional preprocessing step, which would invalidate the claimed evaluation as a unified framework.
